newsitem.title: USA: German banks urge early debt conversion to Euros.
newsitem.headline: German banks urge early debt conversion to Euros.

text.p: The German banking association (BdB) on Tuesday called on the German government to convert its outstanding debt into Euros from the currency's launch on January 1, 1999.
"The decision (to do this) is overdue," said BdB president Karl-Heinz Wessel.

Although Germany, in line with other countries, has already agreed issue new debt in the single European curency from its creation in 1999, it has lagged Paris in making the commitment to also immediately convert debt already issued.
Wessel said that it would be essential for Germany to follow the French lead if it did not want to lose out in financial market transactions to Paris.
"If we want to hold our own in competition particularly with Paris, then the conversion of all tradeable public paper must take place on January 1, 1999," he said.
"The decision is also in the interests of the public authorities, specifically of the federal government, assuming that it does not want to lose its position as a benchmark issuer," he added.
Although there has been no official statement yet from Bonn, Bundesbank officials have indicated in recent days that there is growing support for an early conversion.
Bundesbank Chief Economist Otmar Issing said Monday that Germany should make every effort to convert the bulk of its outstanding debt from the Euro's launch year in 1999.
"I think we should find a way so that the important part of public debt can be translated into Euros," Issing told a conference in Washington.
